audumbara_node_claims.definition: The amulet of udumbara wood, worn in AVS 19.31 for prosperity, cattle and fatness in the cow-stall, and addressed as prosperity itself. All seven occurrences are in that one hymn.

supplementary_corpus_replay.note: The Wave 2 build's input directory is not in the repository -- it expects flat files named SBM.txt, KatySS.txt and so on, while the DCS repository prints them as 'Brahmana texts/SBM.txt' and the like. The mapping was reconstructed and is recorded in manifest.source_snapshot so the build is replayable.

registry_disagreements.registry_says: Only 14 of 23 registry objects are linked to a rite.
registry_disagreements.measured: 14 of 41. The denominator moved: Wave 3 imported 18 more Object nodes and wired none of them, so the shortfall is larger than the row records, not smaller.

registry_disagreements.registry_says: 11 ritual roles are modelled against the classical set of sixteen; missing_count 5.
registry_disagreements.measured: 11 RitualRole nodes exist, but only 7 of them are among the classical sixteen. Four of the eleven -- PRASASTR-DIRECTOR, YAJAMANA-SACRIFICER, PUROHITA-CHAPLAIN, BRAHMACARIN-STUDENT -- are not officiants in that schema at all. So 9 are missing, not 5. Eleven and sixteen are both real numbers that do not share a denominator.

registry_disagreements.registry_says: MATCH (r:Ritual) RETURN offerings -> 0 for all 8 rites, so no modelled rite is linked to an offering.
registry_disagreements.measured: 15 Ritual->Offering edges exist over 5 rites: {'USES_SUBSTANCE': 11, 'USES_OFFERING': 4}. The claim of zero is false; what is true is that none of them is typed as recipiency.

registry_disagreements.registry_says: 0 mantras carry ritual_context, although 3,045 Wave 3 ritual rows were staged.
registry_disagreements.measured: 0 confirmed, and the 3,045 staged rows cover 1903 distinct mantras, not 3,045: the file is rows, not passages.

defects_found.defect: `apsu` is registered as a dative form of Apah. It is the LOCATIVE plural of ap-. All 20 loci behind the Apah RECEIVES_OFFERING row came through it and every one means 'in/into the waters' -- `apsu juhoti`, `apsu somacamasan`. The row was published as Apah ranking third among recipients.
defects_found.fix: Remove apsu; the row then has no witness and is dropped entirely.

defects_found.defect: The staged RECEIVES_OFFERING rows carry no offering at the far end. The offering words are used only as a line filter and are never resolved to an :Offering node, so all 27 rows are (:Devata)-[:RECEIVES_OFFERING]->(nothing). An edge needs a node at the far end, so the typed deity-to-offering predicate GAP-RITUAL-005 asks for could not have landed as staged.
defects_found.fix: Resolve the offering word to an :Offering key and emit one row per (Devata, Offering) pair.

defects_found.defect: Nine of the twenty-two offering markers are VERBS -- nirvap, juhoti, juhuyat, yajati, yajeta, alabhate, alabheta, hutam. A line qualifies as a deity-to-offering statement when it names a deity in the dative and contains a verb of offering, with no offering named at all.
defects_found.fix: Require an offering NOUN; keep the verb as a necessary condition rather than a sufficient one.

defects_found.defect: SankhSS 13.14.1 is held in canonical Neo4j as an ANCHORED_SUTRA step of VG:CONCEPT:DIKSA-CONSECRATION. The rite the line states in its own words is the SATTRA -- `satram asiran` -- and Caland's translation opens 'A sattra may be performed by sixteen persons'. `diksita` in that line is a participle describing the performers, not a naming of the diksa. ritual_registries.RITE_CANDIDATES registers SATTRA with the prefix `sattrayan` and the exact forms sattram / sattrasya / sattre / sattrani / sattranam, all double-t. The Sankhayana edition prints the single-t `satram`, which no registered form reaches, so the only rite alias that fired on the line was `diksit`.
defects_found.fix: Register the single-t orthographic variants of sattra as aliases.

defects_found.defect: The node is defined from AVS 19.31 as an amulet of udumbara wood and carries supplementary_attestation_count=91. Every one of those lines is udumbara WOOD -- the sadas post, the camasa, the asandi, the danda -- and not one is the amulet. The property asserts corroboration the corpus does not give.
defects_found.fix: Split the wood from the amulet, or reduce the count to the lines that are about the amulet, which is zero in these eighteen works.

defects_found.defect: 25 of 769 EXACT bridge rows (3.3%) carry a matched_normalised_letters span that cannot be found in the row's own citing text under any text form this graph stores for that mantra. The build's mantra-form input is not in the repository, so the span cannot be re-derived, and a row whose evidence cannot be checked is worse than none because it looks checkable.
defects_found.fix: Hold those rows out of the asserted tier -- done here -- and publish the mantra index the build read.

defects_found.defect: The matcher requires the matched run to END where a citing word ends and does not require it to BEGIN where the quoted unit begins. PB 14.10.3 quotes `yad indra prag apag udag iti`; the run matched VSM 6.36 starting 87 letters in, at `prag`, so a verse VSM 6.36 is not was credited to it. 1 of 24 reviewed rows.
defects_found.fix: Add a quotation-start control symmetrical to the existing end control.

gap_ritual_004_arithmetic.denominator_note: The sixteen officiants are a Srautasutra schema, not a Samhita one. Any completeness figure whose denominator is sixteen is a figure against that schema and must say so. GAP-RITUAL-004's own implementation_dependency records this.

scholarly_disagreement.statement: This graph holds VG:CONCEPT:PRASASTR-DIRECTOR as a role outside the sixteen while the sixteen include MAITRAVARUNA-PRIEST. In the Srauta literature prasastr and maitravaruna are widely treated as two names for one office, the hotr's first assistant, and on that reading the graph already holds that officiant under a different key. They are kept distinct here because the enumerating loci print `maitravaruna` and never `prasastr`, and because merging them is an identity claim this artifact has no source for. The disagreement is recorded, not resolved.
scholarly_disagreement.consequence_if_merged: If a reader treats prasastr as maitravaruna, the graph held 8 of the sixteen before this artifact and 8 were missing, rather than 7 and 9.
